relevance_note: An exploratory CVID methylation study whose CD14+ discovery cohort includes one identifiable patient with a TNFAIP3 variant: "one of the three CD14^+ CVID patients carried a TNFAIP3 (A20) variant, we performed a separate pathway analysis of this individual’s monocytes".
method_note: Read by hand; JSON assembled with a short script from hand-chosen values. Scope: only the single TNFAIP3 carrier in the CD14+ WGBS cohort is in scope; the other 5 WGBS patients (no monogenic variant) and the 60-patient plasma cohort get no rows. cohort_size_as_stated = 6 (the WGBS discovery cohort in which the carrier was screened); the separate plasma cohort of 60 CVID patients is not added. No label in the paper (role phrases 'the TNFAIP3 carrier'), so rule 6 label 'unnamed person 1'. The variant description is not printed (the paper only says it was 'first described in a CVID patient in 2020 (34)'), so variant_original_string is 'not reported'. Pathogenicity left 'not reported': the paper calls it a 'monogenic TNFAIP3 variant' and says 'No other CVID patients in this cohort had pathogenic variants', implying but not stating a classification. Sex, age: Table 1 gives only group summaries for the CD14 arm (Female n=1 of 3; mean age 35 (22-46)), not assignable to the carrier. Diagnosis is CVID, not HA20; the paper never uses an HA20 label. Phenotype: only the named-group statement that all six WGBS patients had non-infectious/autoimmune-inflammatory complications; the specific complications are not given per person, so all 20 checklist items are 'not reported'. The statements 'none had acute infection' and the treatment statement are study enrolment conditions (the plasma cohort's matching ones are called exclusion criteria); used only for treatment_summary, not as phenotype evidence. Functional evidence is the authors' methylation pathway analysis of the carrier's monocytes, not a variant-specific functional assay. No contradictions found.
